headline: PLS drops another 3.5% as lithium stays under pressure, while the RBA flags it could raise rates again if inflation doesn't behave — a big day for Aussie economic news.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS had another rough session, falling 3.5% to $4.76. Lithium prices remain under sustained pressure as oversupply globally continues to weigh on producers. At -29% on your total investment, the long-term recovery thesis is still intact if you believe in the EV/battery storage story — but patience is very much required right now.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: The AI ETF slipped 1.1% today, dragged lower alongside a broader pullback in tech and AI-related stocks. A news piece flagged leveraged ETFs and AI stocks falling in the same session. Short-term noise for a long-term theme — the AI structural story hasn't changed.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft edged up 0.27% last night to $481.63 USD, continuing its solid post-earnings momentum. Motley Fool published analysis arguing MSFT could hit $5 trillion market cap by 2029, driven by its AI cloud dominance. One of the steadier performers in the portfolio right now.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two nudged up 0.33% last night to $242.40 USD. The big news is GTA 6 gameplay footage leaked online — reportedly published by hackers as retaliation against Rockstar Games. Kotaku and others spotted 10 new details in the leaked clips. This kind of buzz typically keeps GTA 6 front-of-mind, which is a long-term positive for TTWO.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG dipped a modest 0.3% today in line with a slightly softer ASX session. No specific news — this is just the diversified fund tracking global markets on a quiet day. Long-term position, nothing to worry about.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS slipped 0.14% today — a very minor move reflecting last night's mild pullback in US markets. The NASDAQ fell 1.33% last night (tech led the drop), but VTS covers the broader US market so the impact was cushioned.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE was essentially flat, down just 0.14% today. Emerging markets are facing headwinds from a slightly stronger US dollar and ongoing geopolitical uncertainty around Iran, but nothing dramatic here.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google was essentially flat last night, down just 0.05% to $341.28 USD. No major news specific to Alphabet — a quiet session for the stock.

watch_today.title: PLS: Lithium pain continues — hold the line
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals fell another 3.45% today to $4.76, and you're now down 29% on your total investment. Lithium prices remain depressed by global oversupply. However, the long-term case — EV adoption and battery storage demand — is unchanged. There's no structural company-specific problem here, just a tough commodity cycle. Sit tight unless your conviction in lithium's future has genuinely changed.

watch_today.title: GXAI: AI ETF dipping — long-term story intact
watch_today.detail: GXAI dropped 1.1% today and you're down 14% overall. AI-related stocks broadly pulled back alongside the NASDAQ (down 1.33% last night). The AI investment theme is a multi-year story, and one soft session doesn't change that. No reason to sell — this is a long-term position in a high-growth sector.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Solid momentum, hold with confidence
watch_today.detail: Microsoft edged up again last night to $481.63 and analysts are making the case it could reach $5 trillion market cap by 2029 on the back of its AI cloud business (Azure). Q2 earnings were a standout. For a long-term holder, this is one of the more comfortable positions in the portfolio right now.

watch_today.title: RBA warns of possible rate hike — watch your mortgage and cash position
watch_today.detail: RBA Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser said today the Reserve Bank will raise interest rates again if inflation risks 'crystallise' — meaning if inflation doesn't keep coming down, another rate hike is on the table. This is important for anyone with a mortgage or variable-rate debt. It also puts mild pressure on growth stocks and property. Keep an eye on upcoming CPI (inflation) data.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA 6 leak in the news — not a threat, potentially a tailwind
watch_today.detail: Hackers leaked GTA 6 gameplay footage online as retaliation against Rockstar Games. While leaks are never ideal, they tend to generate massive organic buzz. Analysts generally see GTA 6 as a blockbuster-in-waiting for Take-Two. Your TTWO position is up 4.4% overall — sit tight ahead of the eventual launch.

watch_today.title: Iran tensions escalating — watch oil and gold prices
watch_today.detail: The US-Iran standoff is heating up: Trump threatened to bomb Oman after the 60-day negotiation window expired with no deal, and Iran is reportedly eyeing military targets in Europe if Trump escalates further. Gulf oil producers are expanding overseas stockpiles as a hedge. Gold hit $4,409 USD — up 1% — as investors seek safety. If this escalates further, expect oil spikes and more gold strength, which could ripple into markets.

world.summary: The US-Iran standoff is the dominant global story, with Trump threatening to bomb Oman after diplomacy stalled, while Iran signals it may strike European military targets if war escalates. Gold is surging on the uncertainty.

stories.title: Trump threatens to bomb Oman as US-Iran talks collapse at 60-day deadline
stories.why_it_matters: The 60-day window that Trump set for Iran nuclear diplomacy has expired with no agreement, and Trump has now threatened to bomb Oman — the country that was hosting back-channel negotiations. The US says there are currently no planned further talks with Iran. This is a significant escalation in an already dangerous standoff, and with no diplomatic off-ramp visible, the risk of military confrontation is rising.

stories.title: Iran signals it may target European military assets if Trump escalates
stories.why_it_matters: Iranian insiders are telling Western media that Iran has drawn up contingency plans to strike European military targets — including US bases on European soil — if Trump takes further military action against Iran. This marks a major shift: Iran is signalling it could broaden any conflict beyond the Middle East. European governments are scrambling to assess the threat, and global financial markets are reacting nervously, with gold surging over 1% to $4,409 USD as investors seek safe havens.

stories.title: Gulf oil giants rush to expand overseas stockpiles as Iran war drags on
stories.why_it_matters: Saudi Arabia, the UAE and other Gulf oil producers are quietly moving to stockpile crude oil in facilities outside the Middle East — in Europe, Asia and the Americas — as insurance against the Iran conflict disrupting their export infrastructure. If Iran were to block the Strait of Hormuz (the narrow waterway that about 20% of the world's oil passes through), overseas stockpiles become crucial. This is a sign that even the region's biggest oil exporters are preparing for a worst-case scenario.

stories.title: Asia's economic outlook darkens amid global swing factors
stories.why_it_matters: Analysts are flagging that Asia's economic outlook is deteriorating, with the major swing factors — including the Iran conflict's impact on energy prices, slowing Chinese demand, and US trade policy uncertainty — all pointing in the wrong direction. For Australia, Asia is our biggest trading region, so a slowdown there flows directly into demand for our exports like iron ore, coal and LNG. Worth keeping an eye on, especially for emerging market holdings like VGE.

stories.title: US Senator presses military chiefs to keep the armed forces out of the midterm elections
stories.why_it_matters: Democratic Senator Elissa Slotkin has formally pressed Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and JCS Chairman Caine to publicly commit that the US military will not be used for domestic political purposes during the 2026 midterm elections. This follows growing bipartisan concern about the militarisation of domestic politics under the Trump administration. It's a significant moment: a sitting Senator is formally seeking assurances that the world's most powerful military won't be turned on American voters.

markets.summary: The ASX held up reasonably well today, slipping just 0.18% while the US had a rougher night — the NASDAQ dropped 1.33% last night, led by tech weakness. Gold is surging on Iran tensions, oil is steady, and the Aussie dollar dipped slightly.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: A mild dip today — the local market shrugged off the US tech selloff pretty well.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session saw a broad pullback, with the S&P falling 53 points as investors got cautious on Iran and rate uncertainty.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Tech led the selloff last night, with the NASDAQ dropping over 1.3% — AI and growth stocks under pressure.

indicators.name: Gold (USD/oz)
indicators.note: Gold jumped 1% to a new high of $4,409 — investors piling in as Iran tensions spike. Good for safe-haven assets.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil dipped slightly despite the Iran tensions — markets may be betting on Gulf stockpile buffers keeping supply stable for now.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar slipped half a cent against the USD. Interestingly, this happened even though the RBA signalled possible rate hikes — usually a 'hawkish' central bank lifts the currency. Traders appear more focused on global risk-off sentiment.

politics.summary: Big day in Australian domestic politics: the RBA flagged it may raise interest rates again if inflation doesn't cooperate, the NDIS bill passed the Senate with significant changes, Labor killed off the so-called 'widow tax', and a bipartisan deal was struck on news bargaining laws.

stories.title: RBA's Hauser: We will raise rates again if inflation doesn't come down
stories.why_it_matters: Reserve Bank Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser gave a blunt warning today: if inflation risks 'crystallise' — meaning if price pressures don't keep easing — the RBA will lift interest rates again. This is a significant signal after rates have been on hold. For anyone with a mortgage or variable-rate loan, this is a reminder not to assume the rate-cutting cycle starts soon. It also puts pressure on the Albanese government, which has been hoping lower rates would ease cost-of-living pressure heading into the next election.

stories.title: Controversial NDIS bill passes Senate with 'substantial' amendments
stories.why_it_matters: The NDIS reform bill passed the Senate today but only after Labor and the Coalition negotiated 'substantial' amendments to address concerns from disability advocates and crossbench senators. The original bill was criticised for tightening eligibility in ways that could cut thousands of Australians off supports. The changes mean the final legislation looks quite different from what Labor originally proposed — a significant climbdown, though the government is framing it as a responsible reform to make the scheme sustainable.

stories.title: Labor kills off 'widow tax' after months of public backlash
stories.why_it_matters: The Albanese government has scrapped a proposed policy that critics dubbed the 'widow tax' — a change that would have reduced pension payments to surviving spouses of veterans and others in certain circumstances. After months of angry backlash from affected families and veterans groups, Labor has quietly abandoned the measure. It's another sign of the political pressure the government is facing on cost-of-living and fairness issues ahead of the next federal election.

stories.title: ALP and Coalition strike deal on news bargaining laws
stories.why_it_matters: Labor and the Coalition have reached a bipartisan agreement on news media bargaining laws — the legislation that compels tech giants like Google and Meta to pay Australian news outlets for using their content. The deal means the laws are likely to pass, giving Australian news publishers a new revenue stream from digital platforms. It's a significant win for local media companies and sets a precedent other countries are watching closely.

ai.summary: AI regulation is the dominant theme today — the FDA is being pushed to clarify rules for medical imaging AI, and experts are warning that AI is evolving faster than the laws meant to govern it. There's also a cybersecurity warning from a top tech analyst.

stories.title: Radiology Partners petitions FDA for clearer AI imaging regulations
stories.why_it_matters: Radiology Partners' AI division Mosaic has formally asked the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to provide clearer rules about how AI diagnostic tools used in medical imaging — like AI that reads X-rays or MRI scans to detect cancer — should be regulated and approved. Right now, the rules are vague, which is slowing down adoption of what could be genuinely life-saving technology. This matters because AI-assisted radiology is one of the most promising near-term applications of AI in healthcare.

stories.title: AI is evolving faster than the laws meant to govern it
stories.why_it_matters: Academics writing in The Conversation argue that AI in biotechnology — think AI designing new drugs or editing genes — is advancing so rapidly that existing regulations for both AI and biotech are already out of date. The concern is a regulatory gap: powerful tools are being deployed before anyone has agreed on safety standards. This is a broader version of the same problem facing medical imaging AI, and it's a real risk for any sector where AI is being used to make consequential decisions about human health.

stories.title: Cybersecurity's 'Golden Age' could turn into a 'Sci-Fi Movie Gone Bad', warns Dan Ives
stories.why_it_matters: Wedbush analyst Dan Ives — one of the most-watched tech analysts on Wall Street — has warned that while AI is creating huge opportunities in cybersecurity (helping companies detect threats faster), it's also supercharging the abilities of hackers and bad actors. He says we're in a 'Golden Age' for cybersecurity firms right now, but that without the right guardrails, AI-powered cyberattacks could spiral into something resembling a sci-fi nightmare. For investors, this is a reminder that cybersecurity is a high-growth sector both because of AI's promise and its risks.

stories.title: China's Zhipu AI answers 'Project Glasswing' in a shift for Chinese AI safety
stories.why_it_matters: Chinese AI company Zhipu AI has launched a response to 'Project Glasswing' — a US-led initiative around AI transparency and safety — signalling that China's AI industry is beginning to engage more seriously with safety frameworks rather than ignoring them. This marks a shift in the geopolitics of AI: previously, Chinese firms largely dismissed Western AI safety frameworks. If China moves toward interoperable safety standards, it could reduce some of the AI governance fragmentation between East and West, which matters for global tech companies including Google and Microsoft.

sport.summary: NRL Round 25 is locked and loaded with the draw posted. AFL team news broke today with a debut confirmed, a key Magpie ruled out, and the Sydney Swans facing a major sponsor backlash over a club scandal involving Isaac Heeney and Chad Warner.

stories.title: AFL: Fremantle Docker set to debut, Collingwood lose key Magpie, Sun sidelined
stories.why_it_matters: Today's AFL team news has a Fremantle Docker set to make their senior debut, while Collingwood have lost a key player to injury or suspension ahead of this weekend's games. A key Gold Coast Sun has also been sidelined. With the finals race tightening, these team changes could have real implications for ladder positions heading into the final rounds of the home-and-away season.

stories.title: Sydney Swans scandal: Major sponsor acts on Isaac Heeney and Chad Warner
stories.why_it_matters: A major sponsor of the Sydney Swans has taken formal action in response to a club scandal involving star players Isaac Heeney and Chad Warner. While full details of the scandal aren't yet public, the fact that a major commercial partner is responding publicly is a serious escalation for the club. Sponsorship action in AFL typically signals the situation has crossed a threshold the club can no longer manage quietly — this one will be worth watching closely.

stories.title: Storm lock in surprise signing for 2027 and poach key forward from Sydney rival
stories.why_it_matters: Melbourne Storm have made two big recruitment moves: a surprise player signing locked in for 2027, and poaching a key forward from a Sydney rival club. Storm play the Panthers on Thursday night in what shapes as a blockbuster Round 25 opener. Their off-field recruitment activity suggests they're building for another premiership tilt well beyond this season.

stories.title: Bears set to land former Panthers forward ahead of NRL Round 25
stories.why_it_matters: North Sydney Bears are set to secure a former Penrith Panthers forward in a notable recruitment coup. The Bears' return to the NRL has seen them aggressive in the player market, and landing an ex-Panther adds experience and pedigree to their roster. Details of the player and contract length were not confirmed in the article.

stories.title: AFL locks in dates for biggest Gather Round yet
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL has confirmed dates for the 2027 Gather Round — its annual festival-style round where all games are played in a single city — and it will be the biggest yet, with more games and a longer format than previous editions. Gather Round has become one of the most popular innovations in recent AFL history and a major tourism event for the host city.
